findings.description: The reports_archive bucket has no server_side_side_encryption_configuration, so it relies on no default object encryption and objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored without an explicitly enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 configuration. Data at rest in this bucket is not protected by a customer-managed encryption key as required for regulated report and vendor data.

The ledger_exports bucket, which holds financial ledger exports, defines no server_side_encryption_configuration and therefore has no enforced encryption at rest under a controlled KMS key. Sensitive financial records are stored unencrypted by default.
The model_artifacts bucket configures versioning and access logging but omits server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving stored model artifacts and their data without enforced encryption at rest.

The ops_runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so runbook contents are stored without an enforced encryption-at-rest configuration. Runbooks frequently contain operational detail useful to an attacker.

The vendor roster object is uploaded without any server_side_encryption (or kms_key_id) argument, and its destination bucket (aws_s3_bucket.reports_archive) provides no default encryption, so this sensitive vendor/PII spreadsheet is written to S3 unencrypted at rest.
